title: mcp-upstream-token-v1
description: The gateway's just-in-time fetch of an upstream token from Django (plan section 6.28, MC.13): POST /agentcc/internal/mcp/upstream-token/ with header X-Agentcc-MCP-Internal (never the admin token). A request is a user's (Request: that user's own connected account on a per_user server) or the organization's (SharedRequest, CN24: the one account an Owner or Admin signed in on a shared server whose credential kind is oauth); Django answers each only from the vault rows of its own scope. Success and refusal are both HTTP 200 with Cache-Control: no-store, except Microsoft's hold (hold): a Refusal with error microsoft_coming_soon sent as HTTP 409, whose message the gateway uses as the text of the call's refusal; a bad secret is 401. The gateway caches a token sealed until expiry - 60 s, under a key of its scope.

refresh.description: False revalidates current vault state without another proactive refresh; expired or inactive grants are still refused.

SharedRequest.description: The organization's shared account on server_id (CN24): no user, scope shared.

refresh.description: False revalidates current vault state without another proactive refresh; expired or inactive grants are still refused.

message.description: Plain text for the caller, never a secret. Django sends it on Microsoft's hold (error microsoft_coming_soon, HTTP 409); the gateway makes it the text of the call's refusal, with control and format characters dropped, each run of whitespace made one space and at most 300 characters, and keeps its own text when there is none. The gateway reads it on no other refusal.
